profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer at RCI / Serco
profile.summary:
Mr. Kelly is partner in three aspring projects: 

Owner of OneTechnology Plus, Inc.
Mr. Kelly has been working as a contract employee for the eMARS Project Office at the United State Postal Service since March 18, 1991.  During the span of almost 20 years working at the USPS, Mr. Kelly has worked primarily in the capacity of a Senior Systems Integrator, System Administrator, and Software Engineer.  With an increasing bank of knowledge, skills, and abilities, Mr. Kelly has contributed in a major way to the successful deployment of a nationally used Database System that has been running 24 x 7 with over 20,000 users.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description: At present Mr. Kelly is responsible for the continued Integration of new Postal Modules (such as FSS) into its growing portfolio of components.  This task included the Upgrading 2 HA Clustered SUN V1280's used as Oracle 10 DB Servers and 4 V240's used as  Web App and Report Servers.  This Upgrade included a redesign and implementation to high end Computing Class Servers which included 1 Fully Redundant SUN Sparc M9000 running Solaris 10, with Veritas Disk Management, Multi Pathed HBA's, 396 GB RAM, and 12 - 146GB High Speed Ultra SCSI Hard Drives for Local OS management.      Suites, 4 Fiber Connected EMC CX-500 Storage Arrays, EMC Replication Manager, EMC MirrorView for DR between the Dewey and Engineering Buildings Campus and 4 SUN T240's as Web App / Report Servers.  In addition Mr. Kelly is responsible for the System Administration and Upkeep of over 15 additional SUN Servers (Oracle DB, Apache Web App, and Report Servers).  In additional Mr. Kelly maintains all the External Data Trasnmission Services to and from the eMARS Database Production Environment.  This includes the ongoing sysadmin of the eMARS AFT Server and the eMARS Development Team's VSS Server used for Versiona Control and as a Configuration Management System.  Currently Mr. Kelly is researching Tapeless / Disk Based Backup and De-Duplication Technology for Upgrading/Replacing our current Production Tape based Backup System.  In addition, Mr. Kelly, is tasked with Researching and Documenting the requirments for  potentially using the USPS MTSC located Norman Oklahoma MTSC as the eMARS Disaster Recovery Site.

positions.title: Senior Systems Integrator / Storage Engineer / SUN Sys Admin
Software Engieneer
positions.description: Having had worked on the MARS Project (Now eMARS) from the ground up Mr. Kelly was key in the Research and Development and through the successful implementation and deployment of over 500+ Postal Sites with Novell Servers and Network PC's across the country.  Prior to the existence of Gold Tape (now called ACE) within the USPS Infrastructure, the MARS Project Office tasked Mr. Kelly with developing a means to have the average Site Technicians with all the resources required for implementation at their particular site.  Out of that effort was born what many in the Project Office coined "LAN-In-Can".  This was a completely bundled system which included 2 Novell Servers. One server  used a the Primary Housing for the Foxpro based Database Environment and the other as an inactive DR designated server which was also used as a Site System Administrator's Network Management and Backup Station.  Site deployments varied in size from 3 to 100 Windows  3.1 PCs at any given Site.  In addition, Mr. Kelly provided the Network Design Templates to each Site Technician which in turn provided the Project Office that site's specific LOCAL AREA NETWORK design and Requirements.  The Project team purchased and deployed all these components in pallet form to each site.  Once a Site went Live Mr. Kelly was then the Primary point of Contact for 2nd Tier Customer Support / Help Desk with Full Supervisor Level Access into each MARS Site Novell Server and Workstations via PC Anywhere.  In addition, Mr. Kelly created/wrote the Installation Requirements and Manuals for Computer and LAN Components alike.
